references.text: The context that introduces the angel whom God sends ahead of the people, and whom they must obey.
God again mentions his angel who will go before the people, with a warning of punishment for sin.
God promises to send an angel ahead of the Israelites to drive out their enemies.
The Messiah is called 'Mighty God', which points to God's name being in him.
The Messiah shall be called 'The Lord Our Righteousness'; God's name is linked to him.
God forgives sin, but does not leave the guilty unpunished - parallel to 'he will not forgive their transgressions'.
God asks how long the people will despise him and refuse to believe, connected to a warning against rebellion.
The one who does not listen to the prophet's words spoken in God's name, God will hold accountable.
The Commander of the Lord's army appears to Joshua, an angel representing God's presence.
Jesus says he has come in his Father's name, pointing to the fact that God's name is in him.
Jesus declares that he and the Father are one; God's name and nature are in him.
Jesus says that whoever has seen him has seen the Father - God's name is in him.
The Son has inherited a name far greater than the angels'; God's name is in him.
A warning against rejecting the one who speaks from heaven, parallel to 'listen to his voice'.
Both texts link God's actions (forgiveness or intervention) directly to the honor and presence of his name.
